newsitem.title: USA: Olympus decides not to buy Worldtex.
newsitem.headline: Olympus decides not to buy Worldtex.

text.p: Olympus Mills, a subsidiary of Olympus Ventures Inc, said Tuesday it had decided against acquiring Worldtex Inc, a manufacturing and assembly factory in Port Au Prince, Haiti.
The company said it believes the value of the equipment and the facilities was falsely represented and highly exaggerated.
In addition, the original agreement was based upon financial support offered by the government of Haiti along with the World Bank.
Although there is funding for new companies willing to open facilities in Haiti, there is none available for new cltohing manufacturing plants, the company said.
Olympus Venture Chief Executive Gary Morgan said the company is now turning its attention to aggressively expanding the capacity of its current facilities, which are now running at full capacity.
It also plans to pursue other acquisitions with more of a potential for profitability, Morgan said in a statement.

Olympus Ventures Inc said it expects to exceed $20 million in revenues for the fiscal year ending June 30, 1997. Figures for the 1996 fiscal year were not available, and the company did not immediately return a telephone call.
Olympus Mills, a manufacturer that owns and operates knitting mills, cutting, sewing and finishing factories, is based in Hialeah, Fla.
